instruction:
Background: `/tmp_workspace/uart_tx.v` is a candidate 8N1 UART transmitter RTL
(forked from opencores `wb_uart16550`). The on-board USB serial receiver keeps
reporting framing errors. `/tmp_workspace/scope_reference_capture.txt` lays out
the contract: 100 MHz clock, 16 clk/bit, the test byte `0x55` must appear on the
wire LSB-first as `1 0 1 0 1 0 1 0`, and the stop bit must hold for a full
bit-time (160 ns). The RTL has **two** regressions against this contract.

Goal: build and simulate both the buggy and fixed versions, produce a
side-by-side waveform comparison, supply the minimal fix diff, and write a
regression report suitable for submission to the ASIC team. All deliverables go
to `/tmp_workspace/results/`. Input materials: `uart_tx.v` / `sim_main.cpp` /
`Makefile` / `scope_reference_capture.txt`.

### Hard constraints on the main deliverables

- `sim_build.log`: merged build/simulation output for both buggy and fixed runs;
  must contain visible RTL→C++ simulator compile traces, at least 2 `[sim] done`
  markers, with the two halves separated by `=== fixed ===`.
- `dump_buggy.vcd` / `dump_fixed.vcd`: must contain a valid `$timescale` /
  `$var` header, a `tx` signal declaration, and enough event lines (0/1
  transitions) to cover a full frame.
- `vcd_signals.txt`: lists the signal names present in the dump; must include
  `tx`, `bit_idx`, `state`, `clk`.
- `observed_bits_buggy.json`: produced by your decode script from
  `dump_buggy.vcd`, schema
  `{byte_hex, bits_lsb_first[8], stop_width_ns, frame_total_ns}`; the values
  must reflect the RTL's actual wire behavior right now (i.e. the consequence
  of the two bugs), not back-derived from the contract.
- `observed_bits_fixed.json`: same schema, reflects the post-fix behavior, and
  must line up with the reference contract (byte `0x55`, bits
  `[1,0,1,0,1,0,1,0]`, stop ≈ 160 ns, frame total ≈ 1600 ns).
- `decode_wire.py`: written by you (≥ 25 lines / ≥ 600 characters); the script
  body must show `vcd` / `$var` / timestamp (`#`) handling, and must be able to
  recover the `tx` bit window and the byte from the VCD; must not depend on
  `/tmp_workspace/gt/`.
- `uart_tx_fixed.v`: the fixed RTL, **must still contain** the
  `data_r[bit_idx]` and `CLKS_PER_BIT-1` forms, and **must no longer contain**
  `data_r[7 - bit_idx]` or `(CLKS_PER_BIT/2)-1`.
- `fix.diff`: a unified diff from `uart_tx.v` to `uart_tx_fixed.v`, 1–3 hunks;
  the `-` lines must remove the two buggy forms above and the `+` lines must
  introduce the correct forms.
- `marker_readout.json`: `{marker_A_ns, marker_B_ns, data_bit_centers_ns[8],
  data_bit_levels[8]}`; `marker_B - marker_A ≥ 1000 ns`; `levels` must be the
  fixed-side ground truth `[1,0,1,0,1,0,1,0]`; `centers` must be monotonically
  increasing with adjacent spacing 140–180 ns.
- `marker_alignment.json`: `{"diff_ns": <num>}`, `0 < |diff_ns| ≤ 12`, and
  `|(marker_B - marker_A) - 1440| ≤ 80`.
- `fix_explanation.md`: 120–400 words, two paragraphs (bit addressing direction
  / stop-bit width).
- `report.md`: ≥ 400 words; must contain the keywords `LSB`, `stop`, `0x55`,
  `0xAA`, `160`, `marker A`, `marker B`, plus the numeric/term tokens `1520` /
  `1600` / `framing` / `bit_idx`; must reference the three screenshots
  `view_01` / `view_03` / `view_04` by filename; ends with a lessons-learned
  section of ≥ 60 words.

### Four work-in-progress screenshots (under `/tmp_workspace/results/`)

Each must be a real screenshot of a waveform-viewer GUI window (showing the
signal tree, the Wave pane, the time axis, the status bar and other UI
elements) — hand-drawn or synthesized images are not allowed. The screenshots
will be checked with both OCR and a VLM.

| File | Content requirement |
|---|---|
| `view_01_gtkwave_full.png` | Full-window view after loading the buggy dump, with the 6 signals `clk`/`tx`/`busy`/`state[2:0]`/`bit_idx[2:0]`/`data_r[7:0]` already added to the wave pane |
| `view_02_gtkwave_marker_pair.png` | Two **named markers** (named `A` and `B`) placed at the START edge and at the end of the STOP region; the UI / status bar shows their names and timestamps |
| `view_03_gtkwave_fixed.png` | Same 6-signal view after loading the fixed dump; the `tx` bit pattern is visually distinguishable from view_01 |
| `view_04_gtkwave_zoom_stop.png` | Zoomed into the STOP region of the fixed dump; the time axis / marker shows a STOP high-level width of ≈ 160 ns |

### Red lines

- Copying any file from `/tmp_workspace/gt/` into `results/` is not allowed
  (detected by hash comparison).
- The RTL fix must be exactly the two substantive changes; do not rearrange the
  module structure.
- All numeric fields must be derived from your decode script / from readings of
  the GUI; do not just fill in values by hand.

parameters.warmup:
set +e
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
mkdir -p /tmp_workspace/results /tmp_workspace/state
chmod -R 777 /tmp_workspace 2>/dev/null || true
which iverilog >/dev/null 2>&1 || timeout 120 apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=10 update -qq || true
which iverilog >/dev/null 2>&1 || timeout 300 apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=10 install -y -qq iverilog build-essential 2>/dev/null || true
pip3 install -q --break-system-packages --root-user-action=ignore pyvcd matplotlib numpy 2>/dev/null || pip3 install -q --root-user-action=ignore pyvcd matplotlib numpy 2>/dev/null || true
chmod -R 777 /tmp_workspace 2>/dev/null || true
echo "[warmup] SPA_task_12 done"

evaluator.desc: Run the WeaveBench rule-based grade() inside the VM and parse its REWARD score.
